description.narrative: Action pour la Gestion Intégrée des Ressources Integres The focus of this microproject is the development of fish farming integrated with market gardening. Fish farming integrated with market gardening is one of the most important socio-economic activities in theMaradi region. It contributes not only to food self-sufficiency, but also to increasing the cash income of those involved in these activities. The Maradi region in general has significant water resources, which are a source of income and employment not only for the direct farmers, but also for the region's population. The village of OURAFANE in the rural commune of Ourafane is home to a semi-permanent pond covering an area of around 2.7 hectares. Populations grouped into production structures practice fish farming and market gardening around this pond. This provides a high-quality source of nutrition, as well as substantial income for the farmers. However, this important resource is threatened by climatic hazards, leading to premature drying-up and a reduction in fish and vegetable production. With a view to strengthening the water retention capacity of the pond and increasing production, the Ourafane local authorities deemed it useful and necessary to support the farmers through the implementation of this microproject. It is with this in mind that the NGO AGIR has developed the present project document. The aim of this micro-project is to make the fishermen's association more operational, notably through capacity-building actions, and thus contribute to increasing the production resulting from their activities. As a reminder, Axis 3 of the commune development plan (PDC) for the Ourafane commune is entitled: “Improving economic growth and employment, by improving economic potential, strengthening the vocational and technical training system, and improvingproduction in the agro-sylvo-pastoral system”. The formulation of the project's objectives, which take into account the improvement of the population's income, the promotion of employment and food and nutritional security, means that it fits in well with the commune's priorities as set out in the Communal Development Plan (PDC). In terms of the Microproject's compliance with national guidelines, it should be noted that it is perfectly in line with national guidelines, in particular the Resilience Program for Safeguardingthe Homeland (PRSP) 2024--2026 and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). As such, this micro-project, which is in line with thecommune's PDC and national guidelines, notably the Programme de Résilience pour la Sauvegarde de la Patrie (PRSP) 2024-2026, is highly relevant, in that it is consistent with the priorities defined in the terms of reference of the call for proposals, namely taking into account the specific needs and constraints of the target population of the Ourafane commune. It is a project whose implementation is strongly encouraged and awaited by the technical services in charge of the area and the communal authorities, in view of theimpact it will haveon the population's cash income through the development and exploitation of a local fisheries resource. 2.1.1.1 ObjectivesThe overall objective of the microproject is to “contribute to improving the nutritional situation and increasing the monetary income of the Ourafane population by developing the waterhole and rehabilitating the community fish farm”, with the following specific objectives:  Enhance the Ourafane waterhole by carrying out development work;  Rehabilitate the community fish farm; Increase farmers' incomes by diversifying market garden production; Improve the nutritional situation of the population; Create jobs for young people. These objectives are to be achieved through the attainment of the following results:  the Ourafane waterhole is developed; the community fish farm rehabilitated farmers' incomes have increased thanks to the modernization and diversification of market garden production; people's nutritional status has improved; Jobs have been created for young people.

The NGO Action for Integrated Resource Management (AGIR) was created by Order No. 166 / MI / AT / DAPJ / SA, of May 15, 1998 and actually started its activities in 2000 in the Municipality of Dosso. The strategic nature of its actions has given it a great reputation in terms of the commitment and relevance of its approach. Thus, the NGO AGIR has experienced growing development and has acquired a certain experience and expertise that has earned the recognition of most of its partners. Its geographical location is national in scope. The seat is fixed in Niamey. Areas of intervention Overall acting is ready and can intervene in all areas of socio-economic life where it has human skills: Community development: through support that can strengthen people's capacities to better manage the resources available to them. Rural development: through support in the following areas: Organization and community support (structuring, training), Decentralization and mobilization of municipal internal / external resources; Environmental protection and combating desertification; Food Safety ; Education (studies, support for schools, literacy etc ...), Pastoralism and community-based adaptation to climate change
